prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Chicago for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objective “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your case (single tooth vs. full‑arch, need for bone grafting/sinus lift), your comfort with surgical specialists, location, insurance and budget. I can help you find top options near you if you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is a simple implant or a complex case. Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best provider in Chicago and what to look for.

Which type of clinician?
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeon (OMFS): focused on surgical placement, complicated extractions, bone grafts and IV sedation — good for complex cases.  
- Periodontist: specialist in the gums and supporting bone; often places implants and does grafting.  
- Prosthodontist: specialist in designing and restoring teeth — especially important for complex restorations, full‑arch or cosmetic outcomes.  
- Experienced general dentists: many place straightforward single implants and coordinate with specialists when needed.

What to look for (quick checklist)
- Relevant specialty/board certification (OMFS, perio, prosthodontist) for complex cases.  
- Experience: number of implants placed per year and examples/case photos.  
- Use of CBCT 3D imaging and digital treatment planning (guided surgery).  
- Clear written treatment plan, timeline and cost breakdown (including grafts, prosthesis, follow-ups).  
- Implant brands they use (well‑established brands like Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer are common).  
- Sedation options and comfort measures if you’re anxious.  
- Good before/after photos and patient reviews (Google, Healthgrades, RealSelf, Yelp).  
- Memberships in professional organizations (AAOMS, AAP, AAID) and continuing education.  
- Communication and willingness to coordinate with your restorative dentist (if different).

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants have you placed? How many similar to my case?  
- Will you do the restoration or coordinate with a prosthodontist/restorative dentist?  
- Do you use CBCT and guided implant placement?  
- What are the total expected costs and possible additional procedures (grafts, sinus lift)?  
- What is your complication rate and follow‑up protocol?  
- Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia?  

Where to search & verify
- ADA Find‑A‑Dentist, AAOMS (for surgeons), AAP (for periodontists), AAID.  
- Google Maps, Healthgrades, RealSelf, Yelp for reviews and photos.  
- Hospital affiliations and academic appointments can indicate experience.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood in Chicago, and  
- Whether it’s a single implant or a complex/full‑arch case,
and I’ll pull up several highly rated local specialists and what patients say about them.
